results.title: Man to face charges over illegal waste dumping in Marsa
results.description: A man who was filmed illegally dumping waste in a Marsa street over the weekend is set to face charges after police identified him within 24 hours of the incident. The Malta Police Force said in a statement on Facebook that it has identified the man responsible for the illegal dumping of waste in Triq is-Serkin, Marsa, earlier this weekend and will be issuing charges against him for his actions. A video circulating on social media - shared by the mayor of Marsa, Luke Farrugia - depicted a man and his child unloading garbage out of their pick-up truck and dumping it illegally onto the side of the street before leaving the scene. On Sunday, the police said that they identified the person involved within less than 24 hours from the incident, which was captured on CCTV footage. The police said that the person involved admitted to their actions once approached. The person was also informed that charges will be issued against him.

results.description: Australian regional leader Chris Minns will lead an official delegation to India later this month seeking to strengthen his state's economic, education and cultural ties with one of its key international partners, according to an official statement on Sunday. New South Wales Premier Minns will undertake an official visit to New Delhi and Mumbai from August 31 to September 3, his office said. New South Wales (NSW) is Australia's most populous state and is home to Sydney, the country's largest city and a major financial, business and education hub. In 2024-25, NSW and India traded goods worth AUD 6.87 billion (USD 4.86 billion), making India one of the state's "most important trading partners", the statement said. "I'm proud that my first overseas visit as Premier will be to India. It reflects the importance of the relationship and the enormous contribution the Indian community makes to NSW," Minns said. results.title: Historic 112-year-old UK department store closes for good as 'old-fashioned' business leaves high street
results.description: A historic 112-year-old department store has closed for good, in another blow to Britain's beleaguered high streets. Hancock & Wood, one of Cheshire's longest-standing independent department stores, closed its doors for the final time yesterday after more than a century of continuous trading. The Warrington retailer, which had served the local community since Frederick Hancock established the business on Bridge Street in 1914, ceased operations on Saturday, August 15. Notably, the store had remained at its original Bridge Street location throughout its entire 112-year history. Earlier this year, the owners confirmed that mounting financial pressures would force them to stop trading, bringing to an end one of the area's most enduring retail institutions. A spokesperson for the business told the Warrington Guardian: "As you will imagine this is something that has not been taken lightly." According to Hancock & Wood's owners, they had been left without viable options in the face of escalating costs and regulatory demands. The representative added: "However, the ever increasing burden of employment costs, public utilities, business rates not to mention the sheer amount of legislation that has to be navigated has left us with little room for manoeuvre and we now feel it is the time to bow out." LATEST DEVELOPMENTS Beloved UK fashion retailer returns to high street after wave of store closures Water companies to introduce 'surge pricing' during droughts under new plans Average savings by age revealed as over-55s build pots of £33,420 - how do you compare? Furthermore, the combination of soaring overheads and an increasingly complex regulatory environment ultimately proved insurmountable for the independent retailer. The store had built a loyal following over the decades for its range of womenswear, shoes, accessories and beauty products. Hancock & Wood had earned a reputation for delivering what shoppers described as "good old fashioned service," with its "pleasant staff" frequently singled out for praise. Store closures have become the norm in recent years following the Covid-19 pandemic, with major brands leaving the high street for good. Molly Monks, an insolvency specialist at Parker Walsh, said: "The transformation of retail was already underway but the cost of living crisis has dramatically accelerated the closure of stores that might otherwise have survived another few years. "Discretionary spending has collapsed in many categories and footfall on high street s outside major city centres remains stubbornly below pre-pandemic levels. "Meanwhile, business rates continue to penalise physical retail in a way that online competitors simply do not face, an imbalance that the government has failed to correct. "Wage bill increases flowing from the new National Living Rate and high er employer National Insurance have been the final blow for many. The sad reality is this pipeline of closures is far from over." Our Standards: The GB News Editorial Charter
